name: TD Bank
notice: A layout study, not TD Bank: its home page and a simulated Online Banking session (accounts, an account's activity, statements and settings) rebuilt with Golden Grids as GIFbank, a parody name, for a fictional customer. Not affiliated with TD Bank; there is no sign-in, nothing you do here is sent anywhere, and no real money or account is involved.
summary: TD Bank's personal banking home page and the signed-in Online Banking behind its log-in, rebuilt as stacked golden grids for a fictional bank and a fictional customer. Where the reference has Log In, the header's corner says Enter: a notice that GIFbank is a parody, then a demo: an accounts page, each account's activity, twenty-one months of statements and tax documents, and Profile & Settings. Every balance, statement and running total is computed from one set of invented transactions, so the arithmetic holds everywhere, and transfers the reader makes change every page.

reviewed.method: The public home page and the reference's Online Banking sign-in page were read and captured at 390, 820 and 1440 pixels for structure, colour and type; the captures are not kept, as they carry the reference's photographs and marks. The signed-in pages were not seen: the study does not sign in to anyone's account. They are built from the reference's own descriptions of Online Banking and My TD (the accounts view, available balance and pending transactions, statements kept seven years and paperless delivery, alerts, masked account numbers, single-use security codes) and from how such pages are commonly arranged. No text or image of the reference is kept in the repository or published.

real: The structure of the public home page: the line of segments, the header with Log In in its corner (here Enter, which opens a parody notice: the study has no sign-in), the product navigation, the hero with an Online Banking box, the row of products, the reasons to bank and the questions, and the footer's groups of links.

The features the reference describes for Online Banking: all accounts on one page, an available balance that drops at once for a card purchase while the purchase shows as pending, statements online for seven years with paper statements that can be turned off, alerts for balances and deposits, masked account numbers and single-use security codes.

The arithmetic. Every balance, running balance, statement total, interest payment, mortgage split and card statement is computed from the transactions, and a check in the repository confirms that each statement's beginning balance plus its activity equals its ending balance, that each ending balance is the next beginning, and that both sides of every transfer agree.
invented: The name. GIFbank is a parody name made for this study; GIF Premier plays on the reference's premium banking. GIFbank, N.A. is not a bank, is not insured by the FDIC and lends nothing.

The customer, Jordan Ellery, with an address, telephone numbers in the 555-01 range set aside for fiction and an email at example.com, and every account: four products named for GIFbank, with account numbers shown only as Xs and four digits that belong to no one.

Every transaction, from January 2025 to October 16, 2026: an employer, merchants, utilities and payees with invented names, generated by a seeded program so they are the same on every visit. Amounts are plausible and fictional; the mortgage follows the standard fixed-rate formula on an invented loan.

The way in. There is no sign-in: an Enter control shows a notice that GIFbank is a parody and not a real bank, then opens the sample accounts. Nothing typed anywhere on the pages leaves the browser. Transfers, nicknames, alerts, delivery preferences and settings are kept in this browser's local storage, and Profile & Settings can clear them.
The signed-in pages' exact arrangement, which is the study's own reading of how such pages work, since the reference's could not be seen.
